room_or_space: Exterior: EAST ELEVATION and WEST ELEVATION (the two end facades of the house, as captioned on the sheet)

proportions.notable_proportion: No dimensions or scale are written. As drawn, both elevations read as markedly horizontal, roughly twice as wide as they are high (excluding chimneys), built of three stacked tiers that step back and diminish upward; the roof eaves project far beyond the wall faces and the low garden walls extend the base line outward.

layout.organisation: Two exterior end elevations drawn side by side on a common ground line: EAST ELEVATION at left, WEST ELEVATION at right. Each shows a three-tiered massing: a long low ground storey with low terrace/garden walls running out from it, a main storey under low-pitched hipped roofs with deep overhanging eaves, and a smaller top storey under its own hipped roof, with a broad chimney mass rising through the upper roof and a tall narrow chimney at one end.
layout.axes: Horizontal lines dominate: continuous sill and string courses, wall copings, eaves lines and the emphasised brick coursing run the full width; vertical accents are limited to the two chimneys and the narrow brick piers between windows. Neither elevation is symmetrical about a vertical axis; both are asymmetric and stepped.
layout.entry_sequence: EAST ELEVATION shows a ground-level door with a glazed upper panel and a low step, set beside two pairs of ground-storey windows and approached past the terrace wall with a planter bowl at its end. WEST ELEVATION shows glazed doors opening from the main-storey bay (under the projecting hipped roof) onto a terrace bounded by stepped garden walls.
layout.circulation: Not shown beyond the exterior doors; no stairs, paths or interior circulation are drawn on this sheet.
